name: Aarakocra
traits: Starting adjustments are Dexterity +1, Strength −1 and Constitution −1. Creation ranges are Str 3–16, Dex 8–18, Con 6–16, Int 3–18, Wis 3–17 and Cha 3–18.
Chapter 2 allows Fighter 11, Shaman 7 and Thief 11. Hit Dice come from class. Natural descending AC is 7. The entry describes studded leather as an option and rules out shields.
Fly 36 with maneuverability C. It throws missiles without an aerial attack penalty. The wing hands cannot grasp in flight. The taloned lower hands can wield javelins.
Two talons can strike in one round for 1d3 each. A beak strike deals 1d3. With two javelins and at least a 200-foot dive, the dive attack gains +4 to the attack rolls and deals double damage.
A seventh-level shaman and four other aarakocra can summon a friendly air elemental after three rounds of chant and aerial dance. It can do favors but will avoid risking its life.
Combat in an enclosed space imposes −3 on attack rolls. The entry lists Aarakocra, giant eagle and Common as typical languages.

name: Alaghi
traits: Starting adjustments are Strength +2 and Intelligence −2. Creation ranges are Str 12–19, Dex 3–17, Con 12–18, Int 3–16, Wis 3–16 and Cha 3–16.
Chapter 2 allows Fighter 12 and Druid 11. A druid must be neutral good with Int 15, Wis 12 and Cha 15 or higher. Hit Dice come from class, with 9 bonus HP at first level.
Descending natural AC is 4. Weapons use the large target damage column against an alaghi.
A huge fist deals 2d6 base damage. First-level chances are 40% to move silently and 35% to hide in natural surroundings. Both rise by 5 percentage points for every further experience level.
Alaghi and Common are typical languages. Starting weapon choices include stone clubs, hand axes, javelins and knives.

name: Beastman
traits: Starting adjustments are Dexterity +2 and Charisma −2. Creation ranges are Str 6–18/50, Dex 6–18, Con 6–16, Int 3–18, Wis 3–18 and Cha 3–16.
Chapter 2 gives Fighter 10, Ranger 12 and Thief 10. Hit Dice come from class. Natural descending AC is 8.
Forest camouflage gives a 90% hide chance. Opponents unaware of a beastman’s presence take −6 on surprise rolls.
Magic resistance is 80%, including against beneficial effects. Magical weapons are allowed, but the beastman cannot activate their special functions. Other magic items are barred.

The book offers a special blowgun-dart poison to beastmen with Herbalism who spend a further proficiency slot. In game, the save against poison has a +4 bonus and failure is fatal after 2d4 rounds. The worked NPC has neither the proficiency nor the poison.
Beastman and Common are listed. Starting weapon choices include bola, blowgun, hand axe and knife.

name: Advanced Bullywug
traits: Starting adjustments are Dexterity +1, Intelligence −1 and Charisma −1. Creation ranges are Str 6–18/75, Dex 4–18, Con 6–18, Int 3–14, Wis 6–16 and Cha 3–14.
Chapter 2 gives Fighter 10, Shaman 7 and Thief 9. Hit Dice come from class. Natural descending AC is 6.
Chameleon skin gives a 75% chance to stay undetected in natural terrain. Its ambush imposes −2 on the opponent’s surprise roll, or −6 if opened with a hop attack.

A hop can carry the character up to 30 feet forward and 15 feet upward. An attack made by hopping gains +1 to hit and deals double damage when made with an impaling weapon. Swimming is a free proficiency.
Wet the entire body three times per day, using at least a full waterskin each time. Each missed bath costs 2 Constitution. Reaching Constitution 0 causes death by dehydration.
Bullywug and Common are typical languages. Starting weapons include club, dagger, short sword, spear and trident.

name: Fremlin
traits: Starting adjustments are Dexterity +2, Intelligence +1 and Strength −3. Creation ranges are Str 2–11, Dex 8–18, Con 4–13, Int 6–18, Wis 3–16 and Cha 3–18.
Chapter 2 gives Mage 10, Illusionist 10 and Thief 12. Hit Dice come from class. It is a roughly one-foot-tall winged goblinoid with natural descending AC 6.
Fly 12 at maneuverability class B. A weapon must be magical at +1 or better to hit. There is no general magic resistance in the player entry.
A fremlin can use tiny scaled weapons at about a third of ordinary damage. The example carries no weapon and relies on its Mage spell.
The book lists Gremlin and Common. The Gremlin language also covers fremlins and galltrits.
